Custom Next.js/S-kauppa storefront (not WooCommerce). All 33 products ('Tuotteita: 33') render in a single grid list (ul[data-test-id='brand-product-list'] > li[data-test-id^='products-list-item-']) with no pagination controls found. Verified real selectors via DOM inspection (data-test-id attributes are stable): product_card = div[data-test-id^='product-card-'], product name+link = a[data-test-id='product-card-link'], price = div[data-test-id='product-card-price']. Out-of-stock items show a red badge (div with a background-error class containing a

Ei saatavilla

) inside the card; in_stock is left null since there's no positive in-stock marker - treat the ABSENCE of a

with exact text 'Ei saatavilla' inside the card as the in-stock signal. A 'Suosituimmat tuotteet' horizontal carousel also exists near the top of the page using the same a[data-test-id='product-card-link'] pattern but wrapped in a scrollable

    - scope selectors to ul[data-test-id='brand-product-list'] to avoid duplicate/overlapping matches from that carousel. Ticket 18: the text_map selector was '.background-error p', which never matched; the real class is 'bg-color-background-error'. The stored fixture now reads 29 in stock, 4 sold out instead of everything in stock. 2026-09-02: source_url moved off the brand page onto the kerailykortit-ja-tuotteet category with filters=[{onlyInStock:true},{brand:'Pokémon TCG'}]. Same selectors, 24 products, all priced. The onlyInStock filter means the page can only ever show in-stock items, so 'Ei saatavilla' never appears and the availability read is in_stock by construction: an item going out of stock drops off the page instead of flipping state, and back_in_stock can never fire here. Dropping onlyInStock from the filter list returns 34 products, 31 in stock and 3 'Ei saatavilla', which is the variant to use if restock events matter more than a shorter list.
